content: Fluconazole is a medication primarily used to treat vaginal yeast infections. It functions by inhibiting the growth of common types of vaginal yeast (fungus). Instructions for Use: Before starting fluconazole, read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist. This should also be done each time you receive a refill. In Canada, some brands of this medication are available without a prescription. The effects of fluconazole persist for several days after administration. Potential Side Effects: Common side effects include nausea, diarrhea, stomach pain, headache, and dizziness. If your doctor has prescribed this medication, it is because they have determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, fluconazole may cause serious liver disease or severe allergic reactions. This is not an exhaustive list of side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for similar guidance. Precautions: Before taking fluconazole, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other azole antifungal drugs (e.g., ketoconazole, itraconazole), or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other issues. Fluconazole may cause a condition affecting heart rhythm known as QT prolongation. The risk of QT prolongation increases if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other drugs that can cause QT prolongation. Low potassium or magnesium levels in the blood can also heighten this risk, particularly if you are using diuretics or experiencing severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. Although uncommon, fluconazole may cause dizziness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you are sure you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. Use During Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: During pregnancy, fluconazole should only be used when clearly necessary, as it may harm an unborn baby if taken during the first three months of pregnancy. Fluconazole passes into breast milk but is unlikely to harm a nursing infant. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not list all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Fluconazole can slow the removal of other medications from your body, potentially affecting their efficacy. Overdose: In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Storage: Store fluconazole at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Note: This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
